questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed in the syllabus coverage for “Advanced Pydantic Models”?
options: Handling dates, times, UUIDs, and other common types
questions.explanation: The attached FastAPI syllabus lists “Field metadata and descriptions” under this lesson. The remaining syllabus subtopics are preserved in the lesson file for complete coverage.

questions.prompt: According to the worked example in “Advanced Pydantic Models”, which result should the learner verify?
options: POST /products with {"name":"Notebook","price":2.5} returns validated JSON; price <= 0 is rejected.
The app publishes itself to production and passes all tests automatically.
HTTP 500 is returned for every valid request.
Input validation and authorization are disabled by design.
questions.answer_key: POST /products with {"name":"Notebook","price":2.5} returns validated JSON; price <= 0 is rejected.
questions.explanation: The worked example explicitly documents this expected result. Reproduce it locally in the listed environment before treating it as tested behavior.

questions.prompt: Which validation/output practice best matches this lesson? (Advanced Pydantic Models)
options: Validate untrusted inputs with an explicit schema and expose only intended response fields
Return every database field by default, including secrets
Convert all invalid values to defaults without documenting it
Skip response validation because clients can validate themselves
questions.answer_key: Validate untrusted inputs with an explicit schema and expose only intended response fields
questions.explanation: Schema-driven input validation and response filtering make the API contract safer and more predictable.
